I read the whole file (lines 1–234) and checked the proofs for repeated reasoning. The only repetition is small.

1. The two-line setup `have := discreteTopology_range hφ` followed by `have : IsZLattice ℝ (LinearMap.range φ) := ⟨by rw [LinearMap.coe_range, hspan]⟩`. It appears in `covolume_range_sq_eq_determinant`, `covolume_range_eq_sqrt_discriminant` and `IsPosDef.determinant_pos`. It is only instance plumbing. The discreteness part already goes through the existing lemma `discreteTopology_range`. The span part is a single `rw`. A helper such as `isZLattice_range` would be a thin wrapper that saves about one line per use.
2. The line `have : L.IsNondegenerate := ⟨(L.isPosDef_iff_isPosSemidef_and_nondegenerate.mp hL).2⟩` in `IsPosDef.exists_realization` and `IsPosDef.determinant_pos`. It is a one-line wrapper around an existing API lemma.

The rubric excludes short calculations, routine unfolding, thin wrappers and moving duplicated branches into a helper, so I do not report either item. I found no other repeated nontrivial argument. The two existence theorems and the Gram and covolume lemmas each use different reasoning. I did not run Lean or check how these blocks are used elsewhere in the repository, so I cannot say whether a helper would pay off across files.
